title: Chart Maker from CSV – Bar, Line and Pie Charts | OpenAnyDoc
description: Make a bar, line or pie chart from a CSV or Excel file in your browser: pick a category and a count, sum or average, then save a PNG. No upload.
heading: Chart Maker: Turn a CSV into a Chart
subtitle: Drop a CSV or Excel file, pick two columns and save the chart as a PNG; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Make a chart from a CSV file in your browser: choose a bar, line or pie chart, a category column for the labels, and the count, sum or average of a number column for the values. The chart is drawn in your browser from the rows your filters show, and downloads as a PNG image. Excel files open their first sheet. Nothing is uploaded.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your file is opened by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: PNG download
features.text: Save the chart as a PNG image to put in a slide, a document or an email.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: make a chart from a CSV

steps.title: Open your file
steps.text: Drop a CSV or Excel file, choose it, paste CSV into the paste box, or try one of the samples.

steps.title: Pick the chart
steps.text: Choose bar, line or pie, the category column, and count, sum or average of a number column.

steps.title: Filter if needed
steps.text: Filter the table and the chart uses only the rows that are shown.

steps.title: Download the PNG
steps.text: Save the chart as a PNG image.

handles: Input: CSV files, and Excel .xlsx and .xls files (the first sheet, with a notice).
Charts: bar, line and pie, drawn in your browser.
Values: count of rows, or sum or average of a number column.
Filters: only the filtered rows are charted.
Download: the chart as a PNG image.
limits: One category column and one value per chart.
The chart downloads as a PNG image only.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your browser reads the file and draws the chart on your device; nothing is sent to a server.

faq.question: Which charts can I make?
faq.answer: Bar, line and pie charts, drawn from the rows your filters show.

faq.question: How are the values worked out?
faq.answer: Rows are grouped by the category column, and each group gets the count of its rows, or the sum or average of the number column you choose.

faq.question: Can I chart only part of the data?
faq.answer: Yes. Filter the table first; the chart uses only the rows your filters show.

faq.question: Can I make a chart from an Excel file?
faq.answer: Yes. Its first sheet opens as the table, and a notice says so.

faq.question: In what format can I save the chart?
faq.answer: As a PNG image only; SVG and editable chart files are not offered.

faq.question: How do I make a chart from a CSV file?
faq.answer: Open the CSV, choose bar, line or pie, pick the category column and whether to count rows or sum or average a number column, then download the chart as a PNG. OpenAnyDoc draws it in your browser, so the data is never uploaded.
